goal: Turn watchdog incidents into bounded Codex repair proposals while keeping every executable action, retry, verification, rollback, and circuit-breaker decision deterministic.

acceptance_criteria.description: Codex emits a strict repair proposal containing only bounded action identifiers and never an executable command.
The deterministic repair policy recomputes risk, rejects mismatched or unsupported proposals, and maps approved restart actions to fixed safe_restart commands.
Approved repairs are executed once per incident, verified against the original probe, and recorded without persisting command output or model-supplied shell.
The controller enforces a rolling retry budget, opens a service circuit breaker after repeated failed verification, and supports deterministic rollback metadata for persistent actions.

One structured OpenAI Codex call produces both the human diagnosis report and bounded repair proposal using gpt-5.6-sol with max reasoning, read-only sandboxing, ephemeral sessions, and ignored user provider configuration.

Immediately before an approved action, the deterministic controller reruns the original probe and cancels the repair without consuming retry budget when launchd or another controller already restored the service.
Repair budgets, recent bounded outcomes, and circuit-breaker countdowns are exposed through watchdogctl and the Dashboard as read-only operational state without persisting command output.
A manual_intervention proposal creates a bounded review item only while the original probe is still failing, without executing a command, resetting a circuit, or consuming retry budget.
Review acknowledgement and resolution require short-lived exact Control Plans bound to the incident, operation, and current review state, and can mutate only review metadata.
Pending manual reviews emit bounded deduplicated notifications with an http(s) Dashboard link and never expose a direct repair action button.
The watchdog schedules deterministic review reminders and escalations, records a stage only after successful delivery, and retries failed delivery without mutating repair budgets or review status.

A deterministic read-only analytics snapshot exposes 24-hour and 7-day repair outcomes, successful-repair MTTR, manual-review SLA breaches, open circuits, and a bounded recommendation for the existing Codex deep review.
Audit retention is preview-only: it counts repair, notification, incident, and resolved-review records outside fixed windows without deleting or rewriting any source file.
